We start by rewriting this equation in differential form.

$$
P(x,y)\text{d}x+Q(x,y)\text{d}y=0
$$

Starting from 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{y{e}^{xy}-5}{4y-x{e}^{xy}},\end{aligned}
$$

we first multiply through by $(4y-x{e}^{xy})\,\text{d}x$:

$$
(4y-x{e}^{xy})\,\text{d}y=(y{e}^{xy}-5)\,\text{d}x
$$

Then, we rearrange the terms:

$$
(y{e}^{xy}-5)\,\text{d}x+(x{e}^{xy}-4y)\,\text{d}y=0
$$

Now, we should check for exactness. A differential equation of the form

$$
P(x,y)\text{d}x+Q(x,y)\text{d}y=0
$$

is exact if it passes the exactness test, i.e.,

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂y}=\frac{∂Q}{∂x}.
$$

For our differential equation, we have

$$
P(x,y)=y{e}^{xy}-5,\,Q(x,y)=x{e}^{xy}-4y.
$$

Now, let's compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y{e}^{xy}-5) \\  & ={e}^{xy}+xy{e}^{xy}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂Q}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{e}^{xy}-4y) \\  & ={e}^{xy}+xy{e}^{xy}\end{aligned}
$$

So,

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂y}=\frac{∂Q}{∂x}.\,✓
$$

Thus, our equation is exact.

Since the equation is exact, our solution $u(x,y)$ must satisfy the following system:

$$
\frac{∂u}{∂x}=P(x,y),\,\frac{∂u}{∂y}=Q(x,y)
$$

First, we integrate $P(x,y)$ with respect to $x.$ Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u(x,y) & =\int P(x,y)\,\text{d}x+f(y) \\  & =\int (y{e}^{xy}-5)\,\text{d}x+f(y) \\  & ={e}^{xy}-5x+f(y)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we integrate $Q(x,y)$ with respect to $y.$  Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u(x,y) & =\int Q(x,y)\,\text{d}y+g(x) \\  & =\int (x{e}^{xy}-4y)\,\text{d}y+g(x) \\  & ={e}^{xy}-2{y}^{2}+g(x)\end{aligned}
$$

Comparing the two solutions, we see that we must have

$$
g(x)=-5x,\,f(y)=-2{y}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, the general solution $u(x,y)=c$ is

$$
{e}^{xy}-2{y}^{2}-5x=c.
$$

The particular solution specified by the initial condition must have $y=4$ when $x=0.$ These values determine the value of the constant $c.$ Substituting this into the equation gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{xy}-2{y}^{2}-5x & =c \\ {e}^{0\cdot 4}-2(4)^{2}-5\cdot 0 & =c \\ c & =1-32 \\ c & =-31\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is

$$
{e}^{xy}-2{y}^{2}-5x=-31.
$$
